title: A pane's shell inherits the environment of whatever started decade
body:
decade passes its own environment to the terminal it starts in each pane. When decade was started from inside a coding agent's shell, every pane's shell got that agent's variables too.

On 2026-11-25 an agent restarted decade from its Bash tool after rebuilding it. Every pane shell decade started afterwards had `GIT_EDITOR=true`, `CLAUDECODE=1` and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-ts`, which the agent's harness sets for its own commands. With `GIT_EDITOR=true`, `git commit` in a pane runs `true` as the editor and aborts with "Aborting commit due to empty commit message". Nothing in the person's shell or git configuration set these variables. `/proc/<pid>/environ` showed them on the decade process and on every pane shell under it.

A program in a pane cannot tell which of its variables came from the person's session and which came from the process that happened to start decade.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/3cd5690e
notes.text: Jack chose the fix: decade starts pane programs with the user session's environment, read from `systemctl --user show-environment`, plus decade's own `DECADE_*` variables, and ignores the environment of the process that started decade. If systemd's user manager cannot be reached, decade falls back to its own environment.
